intended_application: active and intelligent (pH-sensitive) packaging films and edible coatings

process_steps.description: Anthocyanin solutions prepared from the cabbage and grape marc extracts at 3.6 mg anthocyanins/mL

source.quote: The anthocyanin solutions for the FFS were prepared from the extracts of cabbage and grape marc at an equal concentration of 3.6 ± 0.2 mg anthocyanins/mL

process_steps.description: Reagents mixed with a magnetic stirrer

source.quote: reagents were mixed with a magnetic stirrer (AREX Heating Magnetic Stirrer, Velp Scientifica, Usmate (MB) Italy) at 25 °C for 5 min
the system was sonicated (Bandelin Sonorex, RH 102 K, Milano, Italy) for 10 min at 25 °C and 35 kHz

process_steps.description: Heated to gelatinise the starch while stirring with an overhead stirrer at 150 rpm

source.quote: The obtained suspensions were heated to 80 °C for 45 min to allow starch gelatinization, while mixing was carried out with an overhead stirrer (RW20, IKA, Staufen, Germany) at 150 rpm
The FFS was used to form related films using the tape-casting method, according to previous studies [21], at 40 °C using a knife

process_steps.description: Dried in a forced convection oven

source.quote: The casted film was then dried for about 3 h at 65 °C in a forced convection oven

recipes.description: Potato starch film with 3 g glycerol per 10 g starch, made with 75% anthocyanin solution (from red cabbage or grape marc waste) in place of water

ingredients.name: anthocyanin solution (3.6 mg anthocyanins/mL, from cabbage and grape marc extracts)
ingredients.feedstock: red cabbage waste and grape marc

source.quote: Their antioxidant effect and structuring capacity in starch-based packaging films make the anthocyanin–starch–glycerol system suitable for the preparation of active packaging films and intelligent packaging films
